goal: Build and verify XTrawl, a standalone strict TypeScript read-only X scraper and crawler.
completed: Harness workflow, product contract, architecture, security boundary, and build plan created.
Strict typed client, auth loaders, SQLite state, account pool, GraphQL transport, manifest handling, query builders, pagination, outputs, library facade, and CLI implemented.
Deterministic behavioral coverage expanded across all implemented domains.
Husky 9 configured with a pre-commit hook that requires lint and build to pass.
Project, package, CLI, public client, and public error base rebranded to XTrawl/xtrawl.
README rewritten with a Mermaid architecture flow, source quick start, common tasks, safety guidance, and documentation links.
Detailed standalone documentation added for authentication, account pools, proxies, API and CLI usage, filters, resume behavior, output, configuration, errors, storage, security, and troubleshooting.
Current X GraphQL operation IDs and read-only POST transport implemented, with authenticated automatic refresh and one retry after 404 or 422.
Single-post lookup added to the TypeScript client and CLI.
All seven read operations and authenticated manifest refresh passed bounded live verification.
Added default 30-day search bounds, concurrent interval scheduling, per-page account rotation and retries, lease heartbeats, session repair, and accurate usage accounting.
Added URL, handle, and numeric-ID target normalization, no-progress pagination stops, raw relationship output control, profile saving, appendable descriptive output names, and real run statistics.
Added SOCKS5 support, proxy preflight checks, built-in transaction headers, operation feature-switch discovery, forced manifest refresh, rate-limit reset handling, and custom transport hints.
Added a redacted account and run maintenance facade, strict configuration whitelisting, expanded CLI parsing and verbose diagnostics, and deterministic parity regression coverage.
Published xtrawl@0.1.0 to npm with a package allowlist, typed ESM exports, npm installation documentation, and verified API and CLI behavior from the public registry.
Licensed the repository under MIT and added least-privilege GitHub Actions CI for the full verification gate.
Updated the README with the live npm package, CI status, and MIT license links.

decisions: Use Node.js 22.5+ built-in SQLite and async APIs.
Keep domains in separate small folders and files.
Keep live credentials outside the repository and gate live tests by environment variables.
Use XTrawl as the brand and xtrawl as the GitHub repository, npm package, and CLI command.
License XTrawl under the MIT License.
Run the full verification gate in GitHub Actions with read-only repository permissions and Node.js 22.5.0.
Send GraphQL queries as read-only JSON POST requests when the session supports POST.
Refresh operation IDs from the authenticated responsive-web bundle after HTTP 404 or 422 and retry once.
Send the authentication cookie only to the X page request, never to static script hosts.
Lease accounts per page so retries can rotate accounts without losing a target cursor.
Keep the default Node transport asynchronous; pass mode and impersonation hints only to caller-provided adapters.
Redact all public inspection projections and keep destructive duplicate cleanup in dry-run mode by default.
openQuestions: Should caller-owned account state use a pluggable AccountStateStore adapter, explicit snapshot export/import methods, or both?
Should searchPage expose only the opaque nextCursor or also page metadata such as request count, rate-limit reset, and the normalized effective query?
Should the MCP server ship with stdio transport only or support optional authenticated Streamable HTTP for remote agent harnesses?
risks: Live GraphQL identifiers and platform responses can change; manifest refresh and fake transport tests are required.
An MCP surface can amplify collection volume or expose sensitive state unless tool schemas enforce read-only operations, strict bounds, secret redaction, and explicit caller configuration.
doNotRepeat: Do not add credentials or external project names to this tree.
Do not treat skipped live tests as network verification.
